newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks open weaker on profit taking.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks open weaker on profit taking.

text.p: Australian shares opened weaker on Friday, the market pulling back from its record closing high on Thursday with investor profit-taking guided by the Wall Street which ended weaker for a fourth consecutive session.
From the opening, the All Ordinaries index lost 16.7 points to 2,360.9.
Brokers said the market was headed for a huge volume day as a large number of shares were passed through the market due to equity traded option expiries on Thursday.
"It's hard to read the market when so much option-related volume is going through, but generally the market is weaker across the board," a Melbourne-based dealer said.

The dealer said early business was dominated by the main option traded stocks, BHP, National Australia Bank and CRA. In the first half hour of trade, about A$257 million (US$206 million) worth of BHP stock was put through the market.
"The market has been bullish in the last month and this has culminated in higher derivatives turnover," he said.
The market's record one day turnover was set on June 28 when A$1.595 billion worth of stock was traded.
Dealers said the market seemed to have found its low for the session in the first 15 minutes of trade after a wave of options related business was put in the market.
"The day after option expiries there is usually a wave of trade at the start and one near the end of trade, but it's unpredictable, it could pull the market either way," the dealer said.
